title: Noetherian canonical strict henselization and regular divisor quotient
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative regular ring [def-weil-regular-scheme], $f\in R$, and suppose $R/(f)$ is regular. Let $\bar y:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ be a geometric point [def-weil-geometric-point], let $H$ be the canonical pointed-neighbourhood coordinate-ring colimit [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit], and let $b:R\to H$ induce the canonical structural map [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-structural-map]. Assume $b(f)$ is not a unit. Then $H$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $H/(b(f))$ is a regular ring, and $H/(b(f))$ is a domain, meaning a nonzero commutative ring with no zero divisors. No cover or root extension is involved.

source.place: Tag 0EYG (pione-lemma-abhyankar-one-divisor), strict henselization paragraph; Tag 05WS (lemma-quotient-strict-henselization); Tag 06LN, regularity under strict henselization.

proof.text: Identify H with the strict henselization of the local ring at the geometric point via pointed etale triples and their colimit. The structural map identity determines b by faithfulness of Spec. The local ring is Noetherian and its strict henselization is Noetherian.

The nonunit condition puts the point on the divisor. Tag 05WS (lemma-quotient-strict-henselization) identifies H/(b(f)) with the strict henselization of the corresponding local ring of R/(f). This is regular local by Tag 06LN, hence a domain and a regular ring.

theorem strictHenselization_regular_divisor_quotient
    (R : CommRingCat.{u}) [IsRegularRing R] (f : R)
    [IsRegularRing (R ⧸ Ideal.span {f})]
    {Ω : Type u} [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω] (barY : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ Spec R)
    (b : R ⟶ strictHenselizationRing barY)
    (hb : Spec.map b = strictHenselizationStructuralMap barY)
    (hg : ¬ IsUnit (b.hom f)) :
    IsNoetherianRing (strictHenselizationRing barY) ∧
      IsRegularRing (strictHenselizationRing barY ⧸ Ideal.span {b.hom f}) ∧
      IsDomain (strictHenselizationRing barY ⧸ Ideal.span {b.hom f})
